messages:
nora: Heads-up: our async python SDK retried a POST on 502 and created duplicate invoices. We were relying on implicit retries for availability but hit side effects.

dylan: Yikes. Which version? Sync or async client?

nora: async (redwood==0.11.2). Minimal repro: ```py
async with RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=K) as c:
    r = await c.post('/v1/invoices', json={'amount': 20})
    print(await r.json())
```
Server returned 502, then client retried and returned 201.

cheng: We've historically considered all 5xx retryable, but that's unsafe for mutating methods. Does the client honor Idempotency-Key?

nora: No header set. We discovered that setting Idempotency-Key prevented duplicates.

ci-bot: New issue DEVEX-4923 filed: "async sdk auto-retry on non-idempotent POSTs causing duplicate resources" assigned @dylan.

dylan: Plan proposal: default behavior for mutable methods (POST, DELETE, PATCH) => do not retry on 5xx unless Idempotency-Key present or user explicitly enables retries. PUT will remain retryable by default. Add telemetry when a retry is suppressed.

maya: Also verify body replayability: streaming uploads should not be silently buffered and retried. Instead error or require explicit buffering.

cheng: Tests we need: (1) POST without idempotency + 5xx => no retry. (2) POST with Idempotency-Key + 5xx => retry allowed. (3) streaming body => raise if retry would be attempted. (4) backoff timings respected by async loop.

nora: For now workaround: set client.retry_policy = RetryPolicy(max_retries=0) or add an Idempotency-Key header. I pushed that to our staging.

dylan: I'll implement change in both clients and sync up release notes. Also add a small helper function to generate idempotency keys (uuid4) and mention it in quickstart.

release-bot: PR #1315 opened by dylan -> fix/retry-idempotency. CI queued.

ci-bot: CI passed for #1315. Canary deploy starting.

maya: Canary confirmed: single invoice created in staging after induced failure.

dylan: Merging to main and preparing patch release 0.11.5. Will add migration note recommending idempotency for mutating endpoints and showing how to opt-in.

nora: Thanks all. Please add a short note in SDK docs about the new conservative default and the helper util.
